kevin (Eng): Quick Q 
I'm scheduled for an unpaid medical LOA 2030-02-10 to 2030-05-10. I contribute to Roth 401(k) and have a small 401(k) loan. Can I switch my deferral to pretax or Roth midleave? Also will loan repayments pause automatically? Any tax/catch-up implications?

sam-peopleops: You can change your deferral election while employed. If you switch to 0% before your last paid check, deductions stop. You can't retroactively change deferrals for pay already processed.

nora-payroll: Loan repayments stop if there's no wages to withhold. Vendor usually documents a suspension for short LOAs if benefits@redwood.com notifies them. If loan becomes delinquent or there's separation, it could be offset and treated as a distribution.

isaac (Maple Retirement): Maple note: Roth vs pretax is an employee election. During LOA, if there's no taxable wages, Roth contributions won't occur. On return you can elect Roth or pretax. For loans: email loans@mapleret.com with LOA dates and loan ID; we can record a suspension and planned restart to avoid auto-offset.

kevin (Eng): Any way to "catch up" the missed Roth contributions later? I'm worried about hitting annual limits.

nora-payroll: You can't put missed payroll into prior pay periods. You can increase future deferral percent (subject to IRS limits) to try to use remaining annual allowance. If you're near the annual cap, contact benefits to model scenarios.

sam-peopleops: Action items for you: 1) update Workday deferral by payroll cutoff (17:00 PT two business days before pay) if you want 0% during LOA. 2) send LOA approval to benefits@redwood.com. 3) email loans@mapleret.com with loan ID. We'll schedule a 10-min call with Maple if helpful.

benefits-bot: Reminder: 401(k) change cutoff is 17:00 PT two business days before payroll. LOA upload: https://intranet.redwood/hr/leave-upload

kevin (Eng): Thanks 60a I'll submit LOA and ping once done.
